result:
B14 is built and all the checks pass: typecheck, token check, production build and the full test suite (157 files, 872 tests).

One caveat on the tests. With the default 16 workers, two full runs hit intermittent failures, and each time in different browser suites, mostly ones unrelated to this change. The errors were Chromium crashes and the harness's `clock.pauseAt` failing because a page took more than a second to load. The first default run passed cleanly, and a run with `--maxWorkers=6` passed everything. My three new test files each start their own browser, which adds a little to that load.

**What changed**
- **Card row** (`src/ui/title.css`): cards share one width and shrink together down to 96px. Below that the row scrolls sideways with a snap point per card, no scrollbar, and the next card peeking in. RACE sits outside the row and doesn't move. The row has a 12px padding offset by a negative margin, so scrolling doesn't clip card shadows, the hover lift or the focus ring; the layout doesn't move. On desktop the 96px minimum is scaled by 1.45, like everything else there.
- **Locked-card shake** (`src/ui/track-card.ts`): a click, a tap, or Enter/Space on a locked card plays one 250ms shake with snap easing: translateX 0, +4, −4, +4, 0px, no fill. A new shake cancels any running one. Enter and Space call preventDefault only on locked cards, so arrow keys and unlocked cards behave as before. Reduced motion means no shake. The existing rule that stops a locked card lifting or sinking is unchanged.
- **Reduced motion** (`src/ui/screen-change.ts`): `reducedMotion()` is now exported so the card can use it.
- **Arrow keys** (`src/ui/start-screen.ts`): this goes slightly beyond the spec. When arrow keys move the selection, the chosen card now scrolls into view inside the row (without moving the page). Without it, keyboard users could select a card they can't see.
- **New stage** (`src/ui/stages/track-select.stage.ts`): `track-select--many-cards` shows eight cards (the four real tracks plus four made-up ones using mirrored outlines), with Pine Ridge locked.
- **Design request** (`journal/runs/2026-11-28/design-request.md`) covers two points for you:
  - Five cards need 512px but the row at 844×390 is about 491px, so five cards scroll. I left the padding, gap and panel widths alone.
  - At 96px, a stored best like "BEST 0:40.37" (about 86px) gets its last digit clipped. You can see it on the first card of the new stage. I kept the BEST styling as it is.
  - "BRAMBLE" is 2px wider than the plate's text area but stays inside the card, so it isn't clipped.

**Test for each AC** (all fail without the change and pass with it; I checked the shake tests by disabling the shake, and the others render the new stage, which doesn't exist on `main`):
- **AC1, AC2:** `tests/ui/track-select-many-cards.test.ts`. AC1 also checks that every name's text lines sit inside the card's border. I measured the rendered text rather than `scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth`, which the plan audit suggested, because "BRAMBLE" exceeds its box by 2px without being clipped.
- **AC3–AC6:** `tests/ui/locked-card-shake.test.ts`. AC6 first confirms that a click shakes the card with motion allowed, then turns on reduced motion and checks nothing moves, so it can't pass on `main`.
- **AC7:** `tests/ui/locked-card-rest.test.ts`.
- `tests/ui/locked-card.ts` is a new helper shared by the shake and rest tests.

Nothing was listed under "Supersedes", so nothing was deleted. The screenshots are consistent with the mockup and the four-card screen at both sizes looks the same as before.
